bibliographic.title: When LLM Agent Teams Fail at Topological Spatial Reasoning Under Partial Observability
bibliographic.authors: Heitor Gama; Jean-Philippe Diguet; Damith C. Ranasinghe
bibliographic.venue: 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2026)
bibliographic.citation_apa: Gama, H., Diguet, J.-P., & Ranasinghe, D. C. (2026). When LLM agent teams fail at topological spatial reasoning under partial observability: Extended abstract. In Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems (AAMAS 2026) (pp. 3567–3569). https://doi.org/10.65109/RTFT9958

methodology.study_design: extended abstract with specified task model and cooperative navigation benchmark
methodology.sample_description: LLM-based multi-agent team in a cooperative bomb-defusal navigation scenario with decentralized local observations
methodology.technology_context: multi-agent LLM teams, graph navigation, topological spatial reasoning, partial observability, dialogue-based coordination

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The paper studies failure modes in LLM multi-agent topological spatial reasoning and coordination under partial observability; it does not address conversational governance, accountability, compliance, risk controls, auditability, human oversight, or regulated high-stakes deployment contexts.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the study involves LLM agents communicating through dialogue in a cooperative task, the focus is spatial reasoning and scalable coordination limitations rather than governance of conversational AI systems. No evidence in the provided text covers guardrails, observability for governance, auditing, compliance, supervision, contestation, or regulated sectors.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Scope mismatch is explicit in title, abstract, motivation, and task model; governance and regulated-domain constructs are absent from the supplied text.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is limited by the 3-page extended abstract and truncated full text; sufficient detail is present to judge study intent and task model, but not full empirical execution, sampling, or complete findings.

cerqual.explanation: For the review scope on conversational governance in regulated LLM systems, the supplied evidence is coherent but minimally adequate and not relevant; confidence in using this study as review evidence is very low.

coding.theme: Failure modes in LLM multi-agent spatial reasoning

synthesis.main_claim: LLM-agent teams exhibit limitations in topological spatial reasoning under partial observability that hinder scalable coordination in navigation-centered cooperative tasks.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces and motivates a task formulation to isolate and study spatial reasoning failures in LLM multi-agent teams, including a task model for analyzing map representations and memory design.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text is an extended abstract with incomplete findings and unclear sample size, models tested, and quantitative results.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence; at most marginal foundational context on multi-agent LLM dialogue coordination, not on conversational governance in regulated settings.
